newsitem.title: EGYPT: Mills drag down Egyptian share prices.
newsitem.headline: Mills drag down Egyptian share prices.

text.p: Millers dragged Egyptian share prices down on Wednesday, a day dominated by the state's sale of shares in Development and Engineering Consultancy.
The Capital Market Authority all-share index fell 1.26 points to a three-week low of 384.41 points.
Turnover was 119.41 million pounds ($35.18 million) but the privatisation accounted for about 32 million of this.

The state's Holding Company for Housing, Tourism and Cinema sold all its remaining stake in Development and Engineering Consultancy at 36.50 pounds a share, above the minimum bid price of 32.92. The offer was about 6.5 times oversubscribed.

In the regular market, the four most active shares in the milling sector all lost ground. North Cairo Flour Mills fell 1.25 to 190, East Delta Flour Mills EDFM shed 0.25 pounds to close at 72.25 and Central and West Delta Flour Mills dropped 0.50 to 96.00 pounds.
"But other than the mills, everything else is going up," said Dalia Sultan of brokers EFG-Hermes.
She cited two of the big cement companies -- Helwan Portland Cement, which added 0.49 to 80.00, and Amriyah Cement, which gained 1.50 to end the day at 90.00 pounds.

"They had become very cheap and people thought they looked attractive," Sultan said. "Amriyah's expansion plan also looks positive," she added. The company plans to increase production capacity by 1.7 million tonnes a year to 3.8 million tonnes.

She said Misr International Bank/MIBank had now switched wholly to U.S. dollar shares, phasing out the Egyptian pound shares. The bank is planning to issue global depositary receipts, with Nomura Securities as lead manager.

Other active stocks were Heliopolis Housing and Development, which jumped 14.00 pounds to 445.00 and popular fertiliser company Egyptian Financial and Industrial, which rose 2.00 pounds to close at 222.00.
The index for openly traded firms fell to 561.49 points from 576.62 points on Tuesday while the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 274.84 from 272.16 points.
Out of the 92 shares traded, 33 advanced, 37 declined and the remaining 22 closed unchanged.
The market will closed on Thursday for Labour Day.
